stairs_down: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW original painted source for a forgotten 1993 VGA dungeon crawler, an opaque square orthographic front elevation of ONE stone arch built into the dirty aged dungeon wall. Input 1 is ONLY masonry material reference, input2 is ONLY arch footprint reference. No reference stair painting is supplied: invent fresh physically coherent stair geometry. Broad gouache-painted planes, chipped old slate/ochre stone with teal damp, dark mortar. Arch fills x14%-86%, crown y8%, inset x28%-72% y24%-97%, same centred arch as reference. Absolutely symmetrical centred SINGLE stair flight, no spiral, no side flight, no broken blocks. Steps must fill most of the arch opening, wide legible lamp-lit horizontal bands, enough light to recognize stairs at 24 pixels. Distinct plane of each worn step, not loose rubble, no text/UI/labels. DOWN STAIRCASE: viewer stands at TOP of a staircase at the threshold and peers DOWN into a descending vaulted stairwell. The full-width NEAREST horizontal tread lip starts right across the entrance, and all subsequent parallel tread edges become progressively narrower and LOWER ON THE IMAGE as they descend away into the well below. Only upper tread surfaces are visible, NO tall upward-facing stack of vertical front risers and no flight climbing up either side. Centre line of treads slopes DOWN from entrance into dark below; their widths decrease toward a LOW dark vanishing point. Side cheek walls and tunnel roof angle down into the same low vanishing point. Broad lit pale top edges with strong dark drops between, far steps vanish into black. Do not put a wall of stairs rising toward top of picture. Clean readable descending-step rhythm, centered. Carve one large plain DOWNWARD chevron V into the keystone, pale worn bevel, no painted floating arrow.
